basis_words: Windows and pairs: q3 (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30) ran the flag-false call and then the flag-true call, both HTTP 200, six seconds apart. Its pair compared 3 accounts with a return on both flags; 2 of them carry a fee by magnitude (abs(feeAmount) above 0), so the q3 pair is the fee pair. The ytd pair (2026-01-01 to 2026-09-30), flag false then true, was also run, both HTTP 200, because the rule as first written read the q3 pair as holding no fee; it is recorded and it is within the four-call cap. Household: the round-117 rule (the lowest-sha256 household with 2 or more accounts); its digest equals round 117's; the Orion household id is the dimension household id as an integer and the first sorted account fills the vendor account field, as in the round-117 template. Coverage: q3 SHORT with 4 groups, 3 with a series, one account missing and one series-less; ytd SHORT with 4 groups, all 4 with a series, the same account still missing, and the series-less account now carries a series. So over the longer span the short account appeared and the missing account did not. Fee verdict: the rule was AMENDED by the issuer (order AMENDMENT 1, after this worker's row IRPT_DASHBD-D2-W306-S1 was filed). The first version tested feeAmount above 0, but the source records fees as negative sums, so it read NO_FEE_IN_WINDOW for a reason that was the issuer's sign assumption. The amended rule ties the gap to the fee magnitude, abs(fee), with the same tolerance and direction test, and leaves an account with a non-positive start value out of the tie while still counting it in accounts_with_fee. Recomputed from the saved q3 bodies with no new call: NET_WHEN_FALSE, 2 of 2 fee-bearing accounts tie (the observed gap equals the magnitude over the start value within tolerance, and no gap runs the wrong way); so false is shown to be net for these two accounts. The ytd pair under the amended rule has 3 fee-bearing accounts, 1 tied and 2 with a zero start value (undefined, left out); it is not the pair the record reads. Cause: both short accounts hold positions on 87 of the 92 window days, as do all five household accounts; all five share one account type and registration class, so no class-based exclusion is visible and the cause is not determined. Pace: six seconds between calls, no retry, no 4xx or 5xx. Credential: one Secrets Manager token load, no S3 token read. Reads: the s3_reads count includes 14 reads of two exploration runs of the same fact_positions partition made before this run; this run's newest-partition read took 4 reads. No value, return, fee or identifier is written here.

short_accounts.words: NO_GROUP in both windows. Holds positions on 87 days in q3 and 102 in ytd. Its account type and registration class are the same as the series accounts, so no class-based exclusion is visible and the cause is not determined from this read.

GROUP_NO_SERIES in q3 with no daily points. Holds positions on 87 days in q3; a series appears in the ytd window, where the cache holds 268 position days. Same class as the series accounts, so the cause is not determined from this read.
